anatomy.intro: Rounded stem joints connect at narrow necks, with broad flattened spines emerging from the surface cushions.

parts.function: Each green joint stores water and contributes to photosynthesis.
parts.label: Stem segment

parts.function: The small cushion is the origin of the cactus's spines.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Broad, flattened spines give this form its distinctive ribbonlike surface.
parts.label: Papery spine

parts.function: The narrow connection can separate; a detached healthy segment can root.
parts.label: Segment joint

flowers.text: The papery-spined form is often reluctant to bloom. The underlying species produces bell-shaped flowers about 3–4 cm across.

growth.note: New segments extend the stack, while detached joints can root and establish another plant.

stages.text: A young plant may begin as one rooted segment.
stages.title: Single joint

stages.text: New joints form above or beside established segments.
stages.title: Stacked growth

stages.text: Successive segments build an irregular miniature shrub.
stages.title: Branching clump

habitat.text: The underlying species, Tephrocactus articulatus, is native to northwestern and north-central Argentina in desert and dry shrubland. This collection plant carries the papery-spined horticultural name. Its compact stack of separate joints makes a small branching framework, rather than the continuous column seen in many other cacti.

image.prompt: Create a square 1024px botanical educational illustration for a cactus visitor guide. Subject: Tephrocactus articulatus papery-spined horticultural form, a small branching stack of three grey-green oval/pinecone-like stem segments with broad thin curling ivory paper-like spines. Accurate species silhouette, not flat prickly-pear pads. Warm ivory background, clean accurate pen-and-watercolor style, muted forest-green/sage/ochre palette, generous whitespace, specimen centered. Exactly four large legible numbered markers with fine clear leader lines: 1 points to a grey-green succulent stem segment; 2 points to a small round areole on the segment surface; 3 points to a broad flat curling papery spine emerging from an areole; 4 points to the narrow joint joining two segments. Numbers 1,2,3,4 only, each once. No title, no words, no decorative border, no flowers, no graft, no roots, no watering icons or calendar. Marker numbers and endpoints must be easy to read at 350px display width. Drawing is explanatory anatomy rather than a portrait of a measured individual.

lookalikes.name: Eve's needle
lookalikes.text: Eve's needle has long pointed leaves and elongated cylindrical branches, rather than papery spines on short joints.

mature.text: An older plant becomes an irregular branching stack. Segment loss and new rooting continually reshape the clump.
